newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI, Brazil's Odebrecht in shaft project.
newsitem.headline: JCI, Brazil's Odebrecht in shaft project.

text.p: JCI Ltd said on Friday it had signed a 177 million rand contract with Brazilian company Construtora Norbeto Odebrecht SA for the sinking and construction of the new Number One shaft at its HJ Joel Gold Mining Co Ltd gold mine.
JCI said in a statement the contract was signed on December 10 and sinking of the shaft is expected to begin in May next year.
"The contract for the project, which is due for completion by April 23, 2001, is valued at 177 million rand and sinking of the shaft is expected to begin on May 2, 1997," JCI said.
The contract is with the Brazilian company's South African subsidiary.
JCI said the Brazilian mining and engineering company will apply technology on the project previously unavailable in South Africa.
"Their proven technology will ensure faster rates of shaft-sinking and lateral development and the combined effect will be to lower overall costs of sinking the shaft," JCI said.
The South African mining house said the shaft sinking project followed a succesful rights issue in 1995 which raised 400 million rand for the further development of Joel.
Joel produced 1,600 kilograms of gold in the quarter to end-September from 237,000 tonnes of ore milled.
